Reconcile its original\\nkey with `remote operation --key KEY --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\n\\n## Read one revision\\n\\n```text\\nremote read --typed --compact --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --context UUID --context-version N\\n```\\n\\nFor an imported baseline, replace the context fields with `--baseline ID`.\\nReads take no `--operation-key`, `--expected-project-version` or `--evaluator-file`.\\nChoose the exact revision and context from the selected inputs or actual results.\\n\\n## Reads and discovery\\n\\n| Need | Operation |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Service readiness and selected components | `remote status --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` |\\n| Local wheel metadata | `identity` |\\n| Captured calls/failures so far | `observations`; includes recovered and denied native calls, no content verdict |\\n| Complete released instruction sections | `instructions --section \\\"RESOURCE_ID#HEADING\\\"`; repeat for up to 12 sections |\\n| One unknown input location | `find-file BASENAME --under RELATIVE_DIRECTORY/` |\\n| One exact inventory entry | `lookup-file RELATIVE_NAME` |\\n| One saved JSON field | `read-json ABSOLUTE_FILE --pointer '\\\"/field\\\"'`; omit pointer for root; optional `--keys` |\\n| A raw base64 field | Add `--decode-base64` to that field read |\\n| One text file or independent reads together | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE [ABSOLUTE_FILE ...]`; up to eight selected inventoried inputs, the launcher-pinned task.md, or work files, at most 64 KiB output |\\n| Recover a truncated text read | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE --offset 0 --limit 4096`; one file, character offsets; continue from next_offset until complete is true |\\n\\nFor `instructions`, use canonical IDs such as `docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#read-this-when`. The earlier `released-resources/` inventory prefix also works. Request known sections together.\\nFor authoring checklists and the repeated released 0.22.1 continuation heading,\\nuse the exact selectors in the selected plugin's `change/references/hosted-drafts.md`.\\n\\nFor known paths, use them directly. Inventory names are relative to the staged\\ninputs directory: `released-resources/docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`,\\n`source/src/greeting.py`, `client-help/create-artifact.txt`. **Do not add `inputs/`\\nto these names.** Native Read takes the absolute path, not an inventory name.\\nA digest or lookup is not a content read. Batch independent reads when their exact\\npaths are known. Unknown headings must not be guessed;\\nread the named file once to locate its actual headings. Request known current\\nsections together and reuse unchanged content. A full inventory is not required.\\n\\nSource inspection and test execution are different actions. Drafting a verification\\ncontract describes future checks; it does not require running them. If the task\\nauthorizes execution, use [Execution tools](native-execution-tools.md).\\n\\n## Other operations\\n\\nRaw mode remains `remote OPERATION --request ABSOLUTE_FILE --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\nUse it for operations without typed input, or when explicitly checking a raw\\ncontract. Original schemas are under `reference/server/contracts/`. Selected\\nschema views use `schemas/remote-v1/OPERATION.json` or `schemas/read-v1/OPERATION.json`.\\nEach view retains its original pointer/digest. Lifecycle test-copy schemas are\\nseparate; do not load them for drafting alone. `--key` reads a receipt, not a document.\\n\\nUse `observations` before the final failure report. It reads existing native event/command captures and identifies the snapshot boundary; subsequent report writes are not yet counted. Keep its paths as evidence instead of copying every command. It supplies no draft text, content judgement or lifecycle decision.\\n\\nRetain failed calls and recoveries. Template admission is not a content review.\\nReport only inspected facts and actual outcomes; distinguish unresolved content\\nfrom a completed definition. Do not claim an exhaustive failure count from memory.\\n\"}\r\n",

Replace `ARTIFACT-ID` in the second\\ncommand with the first command's `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nThe preview writes nothing and does not reserve an ID. Creation writes one\\nincomplete template and returns its path. Content completion is a separate\\nediting action. The JSON output does not contain the authoring checklist.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each missing definition has a completed draft with an ID and\\npath. Unresolved choices are identified. If no definitions are missing,\\nrecord `None needed` in the transient inventory.\\n\\n**Later use:** These definitions supply the verification contracts (VER) in\\n[Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified) and the governing links in work orders (WO) in [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Their acceptance\\nis handled in the authorization process.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c38865671a81429dd291d9f9bb333deae02a4098d4afcf034f293ee919e990e0\"}, {\"heading\": \"define-how-the-result-will-be-verified\", \"title\": \"Define how the result will be verified\", \"anchor\": \"define-how-the-result-will-be-verified\", \"start_line\": 109, \"end_line\": 165, \"content\": \"### Define how the result will be verified\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected requirements (REQ), specifications (SPEC), proposed\\namendments, and existing verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New or updated verification contracts (VER) in\\n  `draft` where coverage is missing. None created or modified where existing\\n  contracts provide unchanged coverage. Accepted contracts remain unchanged.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused verification\\n  contracts (VER), any amendment proposals prepared through [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions), coverage\\n  gaps, and unresolved questions. Retain these under the same conditions\\n  as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read each selected requirement's (REQ) acceptance criteria and linked\\n   specifications (SPEC).\\n2. Compare those criteria with the existing verification contracts (VER).\\n3. Select unchanged contracts that cover the proposed behavior.\\n4. For each coverage gap, create a verification contract (VER) with the\\n   commands below, or use [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions) to propose an amendment to an existing one.\\n5. Complete `Requirement-to-evidence matrix`. For each requirement (REQ),\\n   record its ID, method, case or evidence, and pass condition. Use `test`,\\n   `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration` as the method.\\n6. Specify the inputs, platform, evaluator, and command or manual actions for\\n   each check. Derive expected results from the requirement (REQ) and\\n   specification (SPEC), not from candidate output.\\n7. Set `[relations].verifies` to the covered requirement (REQ) IDs.\\n8. Complete `Independence`, `Evidence retention`, and applicable assessment\\n   sections in each new or edited draft.\\n9. Apply `## verification` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n10. Retain questions about missing criteria or methods for [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec).\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor each new verification contract (VER), run the creation sequence from\\n[Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions) with these arguments. Inspect the preview before creation; replace\\n`VER-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --id VER-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nNo harness command writes the verification method or pass criteria. The human\\nor agent completes that content. No verification record (VREC) is created here.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every selected requirement (REQ) has a defined verification\\nmethod and pass condition, or an explicit unresolved question. Each proposed\\ncheck identifies how to perform it and where its evidence will be retained.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) links these contracts to work orders (WO). The execution\\nand verification processes later perform the checks and assess the evidence.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"16a9ea7323450e244b26edd2d1ad757048124b627bcfffa157c8b173f57f363c\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release or operating contract\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"start_line\": 166, \"end_line\": 220, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release or operating contract\\n\\n**Inputs:** A proposed release or ongoing operating obligation, its scope,\\nexisting work-order or requirement IDs, and any accepted contract that may\\nalready cover it.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** A completed release-contract (REL) or operating-contract\\n  (OPS) draft when needed. An accepted contract is reused only if its meaning\\n  and scope already cover the proposed obligation.\\n- **Transient working material:** Selection notes, new IDs and paths, and\\n  unresolved questions. No release or operating authorization is inferred.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Decide which obligation applies: release scope uses `release_contract`;\\n   continuing assurance uses `operating_contract`. Do not create both by default.\\n2. Read existing contracts selected for reuse. If an accepted contract needs\\n   changed meaning, use the accepted-definition amendment boundary; do not edit\\n   it through this draft-creation procedure.\\n3. For a missing contract, use the supported domain and artifact creation\\n   sequence from \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Inspect the dry-run result and use its\\n   returned `allocated_id` in the creation command.\\n4. Complete the generated body and accountable metadata. For a REL, record\\n   release scope, version conditions, rollback, and evidence expectations.\\n   For an OPS, record measurable observability, support, and operating obligations.\\n5. Set `REL.gates` to every existing work-order ID covered by the release\\n   contract, or `OPS.assures` to every existing requirement ID for which it\\n   claims continuing assurance. Do not leave invented or unresolved IDs.\\n6. Apply `## release_contract` or `## operating_contract` and its `### Checklist`\\n   in `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n7. Validate the completed draft and resolve findings within the proposed scope.\\n8. Include the contract in [Authorize the work](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#procedure) for the exact human decision.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nHere `TYPE` is `release_contract` or `operating_contract`, selected in action 1:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id CONTRACT-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The applicable contract is covered by an unchanged accepted\\nrecord or a completed draft ready for its decision. Unresolved amendments\\nremain visible and block dependent work.\\n\\n**Later use:** An accepted REL governs release preparation. An accepted OPS\\ngoverns its stated continuing obligations after delivery. Perform the checks\\nand follow-up actions named in the OPS at its specified triggers; one successful\\ndelivery does not establish continuing conformance. External operating actions\\nstill require their exact authority.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"723a469b890666ae4b1e7b95a6231200a6794e6b792fef8e043ed82bc4f96ce5\"}]}]}\r\n",

-->|decides| ARCH\\n```\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Capability (CAP) \\u2192 Intent (INT) | `derives_from` | Each active capability (CAP) \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"design-simplicity\", \"title\": \"Design simplicity\", \"anchor\": \"design-simplicity\", \"start_line\": 21, \"end_line\": 58, \"content\": \"## Design simplicity\\n\\nFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\\nreports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\\nat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\\nor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\\nidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\\ndisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\\nfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\\nComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\\nrequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\\n\\nChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\\nconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\\na simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\\ntest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\\nboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\\nimplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\\nsafety properties.\\n\\nStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\\nusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\\ncan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\\ncan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\\nor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\\nor dependencies also has a cost.\\n\\nApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\\nand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\\nfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\\nin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\\nis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\\nsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\\narchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\\n\\nThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\\nmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"29e9b6296f39215c4b2ad36659c0674f0b20650682db9aa1187fc97871cfdb06\"}, {\"heading\": \"intent\", \"title\": \"intent\", \"anchor\": \"intent\", \"start_line\": 76, \"end_line\": 84, \"content\": \"## intent\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain the present problem, who it affects, and the outcome wanted.\\n- What is the smallest useful outcome, and which needs and constraints are actually agreed?\\n- Say how the owner will know the change helped; an honest baseline may be `not measured`.\\n- State the important scope limits. Create a new intent when the desired outcome changes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"291e8274f0c400a3d2d1ecdd56f2c10d68ab6cb40f667076a034e44d87c05e42\"}, {\"heading\": \"capability\", \"title\": \"capability\", \"anchor\": \"capability\", \"start_line\": 85, \"end_line\": 93, \"content\": \"## capability\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Say what an actor should be able to do and any relevant conditions.\\n- Does each supported case serve an agreed need under those conditions?\\n- Link the intent it serves. The graph lists the derived requirements.\\n- Put implementation details where they help the implementer; no required `can ... under` wording.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee6452eeeb618cbe10c941638e7f6be38d2709f53e169920c2d3d012c94ce978\"}, {\"heading\": \"requirement\", \"title\": \"requirement\", \"anchor\": \"requirement\", \"start_line\": 59, \"end_line\": 75, \"content\": \"## requirement\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- State the observable behavior and why it is needed. Ordinary language is accepted; `SHALL` is optional.\\n- What agreed outcome does this obligation serve, for whom and under which conditions? Separate requirements from assumptions and speculative needs.\\n- Include a concrete acceptance condition in `Examples`, `Acceptance`, `measure`, `verification_notes`, or a linked verification contract.\\n- Name the source capability and a verification method. Supported method arrays contain `test`, `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration`; retained text methods remain readable.\\n- Replace unfinished placeholders and resolve blocking decisions before approval.\\n\\n### Guidance\\n\\nWrite enough for someone to implement and check the behavior. Use the template's\\nsections when helpful. Word counts, sentence shapes and numbers of code references\\nare not checked. Writing hints never block approval. Optional metadata must still\\nhave a valid value when supplied.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"333872b200842af881c6c22cfcb0631897071421f423885b2702ac6b72c75770\"}, {\"heading\": \"specification\", \"title\": \"specification\", \"anchor\": \"specification\", \"start_line\": 94, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"## specification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain what an implementation must do, including meaningful failure behavior.\\n- Is each promised behavior necessary? Could a simpler contract meet the agreed need? Prescribe a mechanism only when it is a necessary constraint.\\n- Link the requirements and show an example someone can check.\\n- Give a rule a stable identifier when evidence or a decision needs to refer to it.\\n- Check that supplied rule references exist and identifiers are unambiguous.\\n\\nMissing summaries and ambiguous rule references may produce draft hints. Hints\\nhelp a reviewer; they do not withhold approval. Existing approved text need not\\nbe rewritten to adopt these checklists.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7aeefa5f4ed363ecdef5185d2b776c6fdd9146ece8e2bfd7ae1ee852f0acf6e1\"}, {\"heading\": \"verification\", \"title\": \"verification\", \"anchor\": \"verification\", \"start_line\": 126, \"end_line\": 135, \"content\": \"## verification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Independence: expected values derive from the requirements and specifications, never from candidate output.\\n- A requirement-to-evidence matrix with a pass condition per requirement.\\n- Cover normal behavior and meaningful failure outcomes or risks; do not invent failure scenarios to fill a template.\\n- What accepted behavior or quality does each test or CI check establish? Cover distinct relevant outcomes, reuse applicable evidence, and avoid mirroring every implementation branch or combination.\\n- Pass criteria name the platforms and the evaluator.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e6d36e5fe7a23845861e67079317f856b4f892d7f17c4f3d4dbdb4476edb7720\"}, {\"heading\": \"release_contract\", \"title\": \"release_contract\", \"anchor\": \"release_contract\", \"start_line\": 157, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## release_contract\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `gates` names every work order the release may include.\\n- Version, rollback conditions, and evidence expectations are explicit.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c9c8d32b5f3c5b73f05f5d2cd120379bb50e81625a8d58d6c4d1ce25529a61f5\"}, {\"heading\": \"work_order\", \"title\": \"work_order\", \"anchor\": \"work_order\", \"start_line\": 136, \"end_line\": 146, \"content\": \"## work_order\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `[execution_scope].paths` is exact: files or component-prefix directories, nothing wider.\\n- `[assurance]` is classified and its rationale names what later decisions depend on.\\n- In scope and out of scope are both stated; the decision envelope says what the implementer may and may not decide.\\n- Stop conditions and the completion report format are stated.\\n- Is every planned change needed for the agreed outcome? Include removal or adjustment of obsolete behavior, tests and instructions within the approved scope.\\n- Inspect supporting paths before approval and assess the supplied plan through [Draft work orders](harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Keep reasons in Expected change surface; do not add a separate planning artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8d3be9bfae6d0679a08544ac587fa73e1a26e026d23373c29e1927e0803e7b8\"}]}]}\r\n",

Links to requirements (REQ) alone are not enough.\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `implements` | Names every requirement (REQ) in the authorized work scope. |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `specifications` | Names the specifications (SPEC) governing those requirements (REQ). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) or Architecture decision (ADR) | `architecture` | Names every applicable architecture (ARCH) and every required architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | Names the verification contracts (VER) for the work. |\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) can declare these links in its metadata. The IDs\\nbelow are examples, not records created by this document.\\n\\n```toml\\n[relations]\\nimplements = [\\\"REQ-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nspecifications = [\\\"SPEC-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nverification = [\\\"VER-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\n```\\n\\nThe referenced requirement (REQ) must also link back to a capability (CAP) and intent (INT).\\nAdd architecture (ARCH) links when architecture (ARCH) applies; do not invent them just to\\nfill a field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e5892787048f79f437b0395f9e1269152ce3d1d1b6fb28994f42849bd12a4f54\"}, {\"heading\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"title\": \"Complete work scope\", \"anchor\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"start_line\": 47, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"## Complete work scope\\n\\nEvery requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO)\\nMUST link back to active capabilities (CAP) and intents (INT). It MUST also\\nhave selected active specifications (SPEC) and verification contracts (VER).\\nReuse existing artifacts where their scope applies.\\n\\nA work order should cover one complete bounded outcome, including its\\nforeseeable tests, documentation and retained evidence. Use exact file paths\\nby default. Use a narrow existing component directory when the affected\\nfiles belong to that component. A matching directory does not authorize\\nunrelated behavior.\\n\\nPrepare this scope through\\n[Draft work orders](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements).\\nDo not split predictable supporting changes into extra work orders merely\\nbecause they use different file types. A genuine expansion after approval\\nstill needs the applicable human decision; preserve the approved history.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"021ca3cdecffebe415ce9df445c0c48e24a0acde7609d25220c0fb7d470e054e\"}, {\"heading\": \"assurance-classification\", \"title\": \"Assurance classification\", \"anchor\": \"assurance-classification\", \"start_line\": 86, \"end_line\": 116, \"content\": \"## Assurance classification\\n\\nEach work order (WO) in `approved` or\\n`in_progress` MUST set `assurance.commit_bound_verification` to `required`\\nor `not_required`.\\n\\nUse `required` when later decisions depend on the correctness of changes to\\ncode, required checks, CI configuration, harness policy, artifact definitions,\\nor their links. These are examples of \\u201cchanged trusted state\\u201d: information or\\nbehavior that others will rely on when accepting, releasing, or operating the\\nresult.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) changes the code that validates artifact links.\\nA later release decision relies on that validation being correct. The work\\norder (WO) therefore needs verification tied to its exact candidate commit.\\n\\nUse `not_required` only when the work solely records or transports a\\nverification, release, supersession, publication, or deployment decision\\nthat an authorized human has already made. It does not make a new decision\\nor change the definitions, implementation, or evidence behind that decision.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) commits an already authorized release decision\\nin a release record (RLS), with no change to the released code, scope, or\\nsupporting evidence. The work records the decision; it does not reassess the\\nrelease.\\n\\nA work order (WO) that combines both kinds of work MUST be split or classified\\n`required`. `not_required` removes the obligation to prepare a new\\nverification record (VREC) for that work; it does not remove required checks\\nor the links to verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ad947ba93cfc84640c82a0b165448ce2c15f04beed36f65a3dc031e4287aab3\"}]}]}\r\n",

A human is a person. An agent is an\\nautomated system that performs work under granted authority.\\n\\n## Roles and accountabilities\\n\\n| Profile | Accountable for                                                                                                                                                                      |\\n|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| Human   | Making decisions on product intent, requirements, design, work scope, verification, release and external actions; authorizing work and changes to its scope.                         |\\n| Agent   | Preparing artifacts and decision proposals; starting, carrying out and checking authorized work; retaining evidence; preparing verification records; reporting results and blockers. |\\n\\nAgents have no independent authority to approve scope, accept assurance,\\nrelease software, or perform external actions.\\n\\nBoth humans and agents MUST follow the applicable checks, evidence requirements,\\nand decision rules.\\n\\n## Decision rights\\n\\nA profile describes who performs an action. A decision right describes which\\naction that person or agent is authorized to perform. Being a Human does not\\ngrant every right in this table. Being an Agent grants none by itself.\\n\\nUse the artifact's recorded ownership and any existing explicit delegation to\\nidentify the accountable human. Resolve a team name or ownership label to the\\nhuman making this decision. A proposed `owners` value, an example actor name,\\nor authorship of a draft MUST NOT assign decision authority.\\n\\nApproval, verification acceptance, and release decisions MUST be made by an\\nauthorized human. An agent MAY prepare the material and apply that human's\\nrecorded decision when authorized to do so. Applying the decision does not\\nmake the agent its author. The selected IDs, reviewed content, target states,\\nand reason MUST still match the decision at apply time.\\n\\nThe following stable IDs name rights and operations, not additional profiles.\\nAll applicable gates remain required.\\n\\nThese DR-* identifiers come from the selected evaluator's decision-right\\ncatalogue. Use the right and exact action returned by that evaluator. Legacy\\nowner labels identify recorded accountabilities; they do not create additional\\nHuman/Agent profiles or assign a decision to a person by themselves.\\n\\n| Right ID                   | Accountable profile and authority                                                                                                  | Required input                                                                                                    | Result                                                                                               |\\n|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `DR-DEFINITION-DECIDE`     | Human authorized to decide the selected definition.                                                                                | Complete definition, exact proposed state, and required checks.                                                   | Decision on that definition only.                                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-SELECT`             | Human authorized to approve the work scope.                                                                                        | Complete governing chain, bounded work order, and assurance classification.                                       | Approval or rejection of the selected work order.                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-START`              | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Unchanged approved scope and passing start checks.                                                                | The selected work order becomes `in_progress`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-WO-COMPLETE`           | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Completed scope, passing handoff checks, and retained evidence.                                                   | The selected work order becomes `implemented`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-VREC-PREPARE`          | Human or Agent under the approval of every selected work order.                                                                    | Exact candidate, selected work and verification contracts, retained evidence, and passing preparation checks.     | One `ready` verification record; no acceptance decision.                                             |\\n| `DR-VREC-DECIDE`           | Human authorized to accept verification for the selected candidate.                                                                | Ready record, assessed evidence, and the exact verify, reject, or supersede decision.                             | Decision on that verification record only.                                                           |\\n| `DR-DELIVERY-SELECT`       | Human authorized for the chosen integration or release-preparation path.                                                           | Exact candidate, destination, and coverage required by that path.                                                 | One path-specific instruction.                                                                       |\\n| `DR-RLS-PREPARE`           | Human authorizes the release inputs; a Human or Agent may carry out the preparation.                                               | Exact release contract, candidate, included work, verification coverage, version, and passing preparation checks. | One `ready` release record; no release decision.                                                     |\\n| `DR-RLS-DECIDE`            | Human authorized to make the release decision.                                                                                     | Ready release record, assessed contract obligations, and the exact release or reject decision.                    | Decision on that release record only.                                                                |\\n| `DR-EXTERNAL-ACTION`       | Human authorized for the exact external action. A Human or Agent may execute the authorized operation.                             | Action, immutable target, destination, prerequisites, and recovery conditions.                                    | Authorization limited to that operation; the subsequent tool result records its actual effects.      |\\n| `DR-RELATED-RECORD-SELECT` | Human or Agent; no decision authority is needed for inspection.                                                                    | Exact existing artifact ID.                                                                                       | Read-only selection.                                                                                 |\\n| `DR-REMEDIATION-SCOPE`     | Human authorized to change the affected definition or work scope.                                                                  | Failed criterion and proposed bounded correction.                                                                 | Explicit authority for the revised scope.                                                            |\\n| `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`      | Human accountable for the artifact blocked by the decision; for a deviation, the human accountable for the affected specification. | Open or deferred decision, selected option or disposition, exact reason, and any required revisit trigger.        | Recorded disposition and any declared paired-risk effect. Other blocked artifacts keep their states. |\\n\\nFor a lifecycle decision, the `--decision` value identifies its actual\\ndecision-maker. When an agent applies a human decision, that value is the\\nhuman who made it. For start and completion under approved execution, it is\\nthe actual Human or Agent executor. Supplying either identity does not grant\\nauthority. Preparation `--owner` values identify the preparation actor, not\\na future assurance or release decision-maker.\\n\\nFor `decide`, when an owner label differs from the actual human's identity,\\nuse `--authority-owner OWNER` only after establishing that human's authority\\nfor the exact decision. Keep `--decision ACTOR` as the actual human. The\\nevaluator checks that OWNER holds the existing decision right and records it\\nseparately as `authority_owner`. With the option absent, ACTOR must itself\\nmatch an eligible owner. The command does not authenticate either claim or\\ngrant consent. Do not infer a binding from the decision's own owners, an\\nearlier approval, Git configuration or the agent's identity.\\n\\nSilence, elapsed time, a commit, a pull request, tool execution, or a passing\\ncheck MUST NOT count as a human decision. A rejection MUST include a non-empty\\nreason. Supersession MUST name exactly one eligible successor. The decision\\nand its resulting state MUST remain specific to the selected artifact.\\n\\n## Complete-release authority\\n\\nWhen the selected release contract and reviewed delivery plan explicitly select\\ncomplete release delivery, one human response MAY supply the release decision\\nand authorization for every external action listed in that plan. The human MUST\\nhold each applicable right. Keep the release decision and observed external\\neffects as separate records; one response does not perform those actions.\\n\\nBefore requesting that response, prepare all deliverables and complete required\\nchecks and human verification. Present the exact release record, candidate,\\nversions, payload identities, destinations, required integration, recovery rules\\nand known limitations. Retain the complete reviewed plan's SHA-256 with the\\nactual human decision. Use the existing release record and evidence locations.\\n\\nAn agent MUST reuse this authority while the exact plan and conditions still\\nmatch. A change of provider, a pause or a resumed session does not require another\\napproval. Check current gates and provider controls before each external action.\\nInspect uncertain results before retrying. A changed plan, candidate, destination\\nor scope needs a new decision; a failed check must be resolved, not approved away.\\n\\nThe plan MAY cover future governance commits only through an explicit bounded\\nrule: approved base content plus the recorded decision or specified receipts,\\nallowed paths and a named protected destination. Compare the exact resulting\\ndiff before integration. This does not authorize unrelated work or bypass checks.\\n\\nA released state alone grants no external authority. Older decisions keep their\\noriginal scope; do not add a complete-release grant after the fact. A plan, actor\\nlabel or passing evaluator result cannot authenticate a human decision. If the\\ncontract or plan does not select this route, use its existing separate authority.\\n\\n## Delegation and separation\\n\\nA human decision right may be delegated only to another human who is permitted\\nto hold it. The delegation MUST name the right, its scope, the granting human,\\nand the receiving human. It MUST be recorded before the delegated decision.\\nThe receiving human MUST decide under their own identity.\\n\\nAn instruction for an agent to apply a recorded human decision delegates the\\nexecution of that command. It does not delegate the decision itself. The\\nagent MUST NOT supply a new answer, broaden the targets, or claim the human\\nmade a decision that was not given.\\n\\nRepository policy MAY require different people for conflicting decisions on\\nthe same candidate. When it does, the same human MUST NOT hold both decisions\\nfor that candidate. A human MUST NOT approve their own architecture decision\\nassessment unless they explicitly hold approval authority for that artifact\\nand the separation rules permit it. Drafting an assessment grants no such\\nright.\\n\\nWhen the accountable human or required authority is absent or ambiguous, stop\\nthe affected decision. State the exact right and artifact needing an owner.\\nDo not substitute an available human or agent merely to fill the field.\\n\\n## Authority from work approval\\n\\nWork-order approval authorizes execution of its approved scope: start,\\nimplementation, local edits and commits, required checks, evidence capture,\\ncompletion recording, and required verification-record preparation. A Human\\nand an Agent MUST use the same local approval, scope, and evidence checks.\\nContinue these operations without asking for the same permission again while\\ntheir scope and conditions still match. Record execution under the actual\\nexecutor's identity.\\n\\nApproval leaves the work order `approved` until its start transition is\\napplied. Selecting and scheduling work remain explicit. New approvals need\\nno separate execution delegation table or second start approval. A preliminary\\nmerge and live CI are not local execution requirements; CI still applies at\\nintegration and publication.\\n\\nThe grant does not include changed scope, acceptance of the result, release,\\nmerge, publication, or other external action. Reuse an existing explicit\\nauthorization for such an action only when its exact target and conditions\\nstill match.\\n\\nHistorical approvals keep their original meaning. Earlier explicit execution\\ngrants remain usable under the same scope checks. An older approval without\\nsuch a grant needs an authorized amendment for the remaining execution.\\nCurrent metadata or an actor label MUST NOT manufacture that historical grant.\\nIf the installed release cannot record the required authorization, stop the\\nremaining execution and report the missing historical grant and the lack of\\na supported amendment operation. Do not insert invented grant fields or\\nrewrite the old approval.\\n\\n## Review publication authority\\n\\nFor work delivered through a PR, request the review-publication grant explicitly\\nwith work approval. Name the selected work, destination repository, source\\nbranch and target branch. The grant covers pushing that bounded work and its\\nevidence, creating or updating its draft PR, pushing the later recorded\\nverification decision, and marking the PR ready after that decision is remote.\\nOne human reply may approve implementation and these publication actions.\\nOrdinary work approval alone does not supply the publication grant.\\n\\nThe final commit is not known at work approval. Before each external operation,\\nresolve its full commit and check that the changed content, selected records,\\nbranch and destination remain within the granted scope. Preserve required\\ngates and provider controls. Reuse the grant while those conditions match.\\nObtain only missing authority; a changed destination or scope is not covered.\\nRecord the actual grant in the existing decision envelope and transition reason,\\nnot a new authority file. Historical approvals keep their original meaning.\\n\\nReview publication leaves the VREC ready. It grants no verification, merge,\\nforce-push, release, tag or deployment authority. The human decides verification\\nafter the review package is accessible. Publishing that recorded decision uses\\nthe existing grant; it does not turn verification into permission to merge.\\nFollow [Publish the review package](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-review-package)\\nand [Publish the verification decision](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-verification-decision).\\n\\n<!-- Migration requirement: the released machine contract still contains\\nlegacy owner labels. Preserve its decision-right IDs and actual human\\nidentities. Update machine labels and their consumers in the governed release\\nmigration; this two-profile table does not silently rewrite installed JSON. -->\\n\"}, {\"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-lifecycle-native26-20261010\\\\codex-211\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"sha256\": \"991b526d6280554dcca6901c1790e5519b8894e08635a1f10618aa84a29aaf28\", \"bytes\": 15212, \"text\": \"# Authorize the work\\n\\n## Read this when\\n\\nThe proposed package needs validation, review or a human authorization decision.\\n\\n## Before this action\\n\\nFor reviewing each definition, use its selected [Type checklist](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#type-checklists). Before review, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). Before approving work, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). For an open or deferred decision, read [RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions).\\n\\n## 2. Authorize the work\\n\\n**When:** The proposed definitions and work orders (WO) are ready for review.\\n\\n**Inputs:** The proposed artifacts, their validation results, and unresolved\\ndecisions (DEC) or amendment proposals.\\n\\n**Output:** Explicit decisions on the selected definitions and work orders\\n(WO), recorded through permitted transitions. Work orders (WO) may become\\n`approved`; approval does not start execution.\\n\\n**Steps:**\\n\\n1. [Assess the proposed artifact package](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#assess-the-proposed-artifact-package).\\n2. [Resolve approval blockers](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers).\\n3. [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision).\\n4. [Apply the selected transitions](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#apply-the-selected-transitions).\\n5. [Confirm the authorization result](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#confirm-the-authorization-result).\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n### Assess the proposed artifact package\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected work order (WO) IDs, proposed definitions, validation\\nresults, and existing decision records (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None created or modified.\\n- **Transient working material:** A review list identifying the selected\\n  artifacts, their states, applicable checks, and reported blockers.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run validation for the repository.\\n2. Inspect each selected work order (WO) with the command below.\\n3. Read the work order (WO) and its returned reading manifest.\\n4. Review the governing definitions against the relevant checklists in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n5. Check that the proposed work has defined scope, verification coverage,\\n   assurance classification, and accountable humans for the required decisions.\\n6. List the blockers affecting the selected package. Keep unrelated findings\\n   separate.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint transition --target approved --json\\n```\\n\\nRead the result of each required check. A `pass` satisfies that check only;\\nit does not approve the artifacts or authorize implementation. If a required\\ncheck returns `fail` or `not_assessable`, report its identifier and stated\\nreason, then follow \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d Do not proceed with the\\naffected approval.\\n\\nThe last command evaluates work-order approval gates. A checkpoint-free\\n`check` only reports lifecycle context. Definition artifacts cannot be selected\\nwith `check`; their transition gates are evaluated by the previews in [Apply the selected transitions](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#apply-the-selected-transitions).\\n\\nBefore proposing a definition for approval, resolve its template placeholders.\\nIf it contains an `Open decisions` section, confirm that no unresolved decision\\nremains before setting that section to `None`. Do not remove an unresolved\\nquestion merely to make validation pass.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected package has an explicit list of review findings\\nand approval blockers. No approval is inferred from these checks.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Resolve approval blockers](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers) resolves the blockers. [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) presents the package for a\\nhuman decision.\\n\\n### Resolve approval blockers\\n\\n**Inputs:** The findings from [Assess the proposed artifact package](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#assess-the-proposed-artifact-package) and the affected draft artifacts or\\npending decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Corrected drafts within the proposed scope. Where an\\n  actual human decision is supplied, the selected decision (DEC) receives its\\n  disposition. A paired risk (RISK) may change through that same operation.\\n- **Transient working material:** The resolution of each finding and any\\n  remaining dependency requiring an amendment or another human decision.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Correct incomplete or inconsistent draft content within the requested scope.\\n2. Return an accepted-definition change to the amendment procedure in\\n   \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Do not edit accepted authority to clear a check.\\n3. For a blocking decision (DEC), inspect its current question and options.\\n4. Obtain the accountable human's exact answer if it has not already been given.\\n5. Preview that disposition with the command below.\\n6. Apply the same command with `--apply` only if its inputs match the actual\\n   decision and the preview passes.\\n7. Read back the decision (DEC) and any paired risk (RISK).\\n8. Rerun the checks affected by the corrections. Preserve unresolved blockers.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a declared option ID. Add `--revisit \\\"Trigger\\\"` for acceptance of a\\ndeviation. A risk-mitigation option also requires `--mitigated-by WO-ID` for\\neach selected mitigating work order (WO). For a risk-avoidance option, use\\n`--avoided-by ARTIFACT-ID` when naming a separate architecture decision (ADR)\\nor decision (DEC). Review the returned operation before applying it.\\n\\nACTOR is the actual human who made the decision. If that human acts under an\\nexisting owner label, first resolve their authority under\\n[Decision rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights), then add\\n`--authority-owner OWNER` to both preview and apply. For example, a human\\nnamed `mmzen` acting under `engineering-owner` uses\\n`--decision mmzen --authority-owner engineering-owner`. Do not put the owner\\nlabel in place of the human. Neither string authenticates the decision.\\nOWNER must be non-blank printable text of at most 128 characters and match\\nan eligible owner exactly. An unrelated label refuses without writing.\\n\\nFor an explicitly authorized deferral, use this preview instead:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO --revisit \\\"Trigger\\\" --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nRepeat `--scope` for each permitted transition. For an explicitly authorized\\nwithdrawal, replace the option or deferral arguments with `--withdraw`.\\nApply a passing preview by repeating the exact command with `--apply`.\\nThen inspect the decision (DEC) again and rerun validation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nIf proposing a departure from a `SHOULD` rule, record the rule ID, reason,\\nimpact, accountable human or agent, and compensating evidence. Present these\\nwith the affected review finding. Recording the departure does not authorize\\nan action or waive a required check.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each blocker is resolved or assigned an explicit outstanding\\ndecision. A deferral clears only its recorded transition scope.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) receives the corrected package. Unresolved blockers\\nremain visible and prevent the affected approval.\\n\\n### Obtain the human's decision\\n\\n**Inputs:** The reviewed package, current findings, and any decision already\\nsupplied for the same artifact contents and target states.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Pending assurance fields in selected draft work orders\\n  completed from the human's confirmed classification. No lifecycle state\\n  changes in this step.\\n- **Transient working material:** The human's approval, rejection, or request\\n  for revision, bound to exact artifact IDs, reviewed contents, and authority.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Present one concise request for the coherent package using the decision\\n   card below. Identify the selected artifacts and proposed state for each.\\n2. Present the scope, verification obligations, proposed assurance classification,\\n   its rationale, and unresolved findings.\\n3. Identify the human accountable for each requested decision.\\n4. Retain a SHA-256 digest of each reviewed definition's complete file bytes.\\n5. Obtain an explicit approval, rejection, or request for revision. Work-order\\n   approval must include confirmation of the assurance classification. Record that\\n   confirmation in the work order's `[assurance]` fields before the approval\\n   preview. A rejection needs a reason. Reuse an existing decision while its\\n   reviewed inputs match.\\n6. If revision is requested, return the affected drafts to [Resolve approval blockers](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers). Do not\\n   interpret a request for revision as a terminal rejection.\\n\\n**Harness command:** None. A command result cannot supply the human decision.\\n\\n**Decision card:**\\n\\n- **Approval requested:** Name the decision and useful outcome in ordinary\\n  language. Use \\\"Approve implementation\\\" for local implementation authority.\\n  For PR-based work, use \\\"Approve implementation and review publication\\\" and\\n  describe the bounded grant from [Review publication authority](AUTHORITY.md#review-publication-authority).\\n  Verification acceptance and merge remain separate decisions.\\n- **Why:** State the problem this change solves.\\n- **What changes:** Summarize the bounded changes, including supporting work.\\n- **What success looks like:** State the observable result and required checks.\\n- **Important limit:** State material uncertainty or an unresolved boundary,\\n  when one exists. Do not hide it behind a passing coverage report.\\n- **Your approval permits:** State the exact permitted actions and any\\n  separate acceptance or external-action decision relevant to this request.\\n- **Review details:** Link the exact definitions, work orders and verification\\n  contracts, their proposed states and their reviewed revisions.\\n\\nOffer \\\"Approve implementation\\\" and \\\"Request changes\\\" when implementation is\\nthe decision. When the described grant includes review publication, offer\\n\\\"Approve implementation and review publication\\\" instead. Name the repository,\\nsource branch, target branch, draft PR and later verification-decision push\\nin \\\"Your approval permits.\\\" The human need not type artifact IDs or CLI commands. Bind the\\nanswer to the displayed package and permission. Reuse an actual prior decision\\nwhile its reviewed inputs still match; do not ask for the same authority again.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each selected artifact has an explicit human decision or\\nremains pending. Pending artifacts are not included in an approval transaction.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Apply the selected transitions](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#apply-the-selected-transitions) applies only the transitions named by these decisions.\\n\\n### Apply the selected transitions\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact artifact IDs, target states, accountable human identities,\\nreviewed file digests, decisions from [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision), and clarification answers from\\n[Define the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#procedure) that must be retained in the transition reason.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only explicitly selected definitions and work orders\\n  (WO) receive the applied state and lifecycle-history entries.\\n- **Transient working material:** The preview and apply results, including\\n  any refused transition.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm that the reviewed artifact contents still match the human decision.\\n2. Select only the named transitions. Approve governing definitions before\\n   dependent work, or use one explicitly selected packet for mutually\\n   dependent definitions when the evaluator permits it.\\n3. Preview the transition command below.\\n4. Compare every selected ID, target state, actor, and reported effect with\\n   the human decision. Resolve failed gates before proceeding.\\n5. Recheck reviewed definition digests immediately before applying.\\n6. Repeat the passing command with `--apply`. Do not add related artifacts\\n   that the human did not select.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set ARTIFACT-ID=TARGET --decision ARTIFACT-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set ARTIFACT-ID=TARGET --decision ARTIFACT-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\n```\\n\\nFor each clarification below the formal-decision threshold, add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Question and confirmed answer\\\"` to both the preview\\nand apply command. Use the actual question and answer. When one artifact\\nhas several such answers, combine them into one reason value for that ID.\\nKeep each complete `ID=TEXT` value as one argument. Confirm the saved reason\\nin the resulting lifecycle entry before discarding the working notes.\\n\\nFor approval, `TARGET` is `approved`. For rejection, use `rejected` and add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both commands. Rejection is\\nterminal. For a packet, repeat `--set` and `--decision` for every explicitly\\nselected artifact. Preview and apply must contain the same assignments.\\n\\n**Completion:** The evaluator reports the actual applied transitions, or the\\nspecific refusal. A successful preview alone changes nothing.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Confirm the authorization result](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#confirm-the-authorization-result) confirms the resulting authority and readiness.\\n\\n### Confirm the authorization result\\n\\n**Inputs:** The applied transition result and selected artifact files.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None changed by readback.\\n- **Transient working material:** The authorization handoff, stating actual\\n  states, execution readiness, remaining blockers, and the evaluator's next step.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read the selected artifact states and new lifecycle-history entries.\\n2. Inspect each selected work order (WO) with `check`.\\n3. For an approved work order (WO), run start preflight to assess readiness.\\n4. Report the approved scope and any remaining start blockers. Report rejected\\n   or pending work separately.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the preflight command only for work proposed to start. It changes no state.\\nRead definition states from the files and transition result; do not call\\n`check` with definition IDs.\\n\\n**Completion:** Actual authorization and start readiness are known. An approved\\nwork order (WO) remains `approved` until the start transition is applied.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Execute the work](EXECUTE_WORK.md#procedure) uses the recorded approval. It does not\\nrequest the same execution authority again while the scope and conditions match.\\n\\n## Read next when\\n\\nThe evaluator selects execution \\u2192 [EXECUTE_WORK.md#procedure](EXECUTE_WORK.md#procedure). Before eligible English reporting, read [COMMUNICATION.md#communication](COMMUNICATION.md#communication) if it is no longer in context.\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n### Report a lifecycle result\\n\\nAfter a lifecycle stage completes or reaches a stop condition, obtain the\\nselected evaluator's schema-2 result. The result controls the reported scope,\\neffects, blockers, final state, required decision, alternatives, and next step.\\nThe human or agent MUST NOT recompute those fields.\\n\\nFor a human-readable report, lead with the outcome or required decision. The\\nwording and headings may vary, and empty fields may be omitted. The report\\nMUST preserve:\\n\\n1. The actual artifact IDs and whether the selected operation completed or\\n   was blocked.\\n2. The observed effects, separately from expected effects that did not occur.\\n3. Every exact blocker and every material non-effect. In particular, do not\\n   imply approval, a transition, verification, release, a Git action,\\n   publication, deployment, or operation that did not occur.\\n4. The final lifecycle state and the accountable human or agent. When a\\n   decision is required, name the exact decision and authority needed.\\n5. Exactly one current typed procedure step from the evaluator.\\n6. The command's argument values and boundaries, or the operative meaning of\\n   the suggested response.\\n\\nOnly complete alternatives declared by the workflow may be shown. Present them\\nseparately from the primary next step. Do not invent an effect, authority,\\nblocker, decision, or alternative. Do not add unrelated repository findings\\nto the selected result. Do not replace the returned next step with an\\nopen-ended question about what to do next.\\n\\nAutomation MUST read the structured JSON result. New results declare\\n`digest_format = \\\"machine-fields-v1\\\"`. This digest binds machine fields such\\nas candidate identity, scope, state, gates, and command arguments. Explanatory\\nwording is excluded. Older retained results keep their original digest format.\\n\\n### If a procedure is blocked\\n\\nStop the affected action before changing lifecycle state or extending scope\\nwhen any of these conditions applies:\\n\\n- Managed-file integrity fails.\\n- The selected governing graph is invalid or artifact IDs are ambiguous.\\n- The procedure needs a work order, but no selected work order is eligible\\n  for that phase.\\n- A required governing artifact or gate is missing.\\n- A required check fails or cannot be assessed.\\n- Repository-owner instructions conflict with the harness contract.\\n- Remediation would exceed the selected work-order scope.\\n- The action lacks its decision right or explicit authority.\\n\\nUse the severity and blocking effect reported by `harnessctl`. Do not\\nreclassify a finding because it is labelled `structure`, `governance`, `policy`,\\nor `maintenance`.\\n\\nReport the exact failed rule or predicate, the unchanged affected lifecycle\\nstate, and any effects that already occurred. Preserve the observed evidence.\\nUse the evaluator's current result to report one corrective step or one\\naccountable escalation.\\n\\nFor a failed gate, use the corrective form that `harnessctl check` returns for\\nthe first failing predicate. Do not substitute an unchanged replay of the\\nfailed command. Resolve the missing input, scope, evidence, or decision before\\nretrying the affected action. Remediation that changes scope, accepts risk,\\nor exercises a reserved decision right requires the corresponding explicit\\ndecision.\\n\\nWhen a correction requires implementation, inspect the proposed work order\\nwith `harnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json`. Reuse it only if its\\napproved scope covers the correction and its current state permits execution.\\nStart approved work through the start procedure; resume work already in\\nprogress. If no eligible work order covers the correction, return to Define\\nthe change and Authorize the work to prepare and approve a new work order.\\nPreserve completed and rejected records. The selected release provides no\\ntransition from `implemented` back to `in_progress`; do not edit a state or\\nreplay an earlier start to reopen it. A correction that changes an accepted\\ndefinition must also follow the linked-revision boundary.\\n\\nAfter an interrupted write or uncertain external action, inspect the actual\\nresult before retrying. Continue only work that has not already occurred.\\n\\n## Read next when\\n\\nAfter correcting the exact blocker or confirming uncertain effects \\u2192 [CONTINUE.md#procedure](CONTINUE.md#procedure). Missing evaluator \\u2192 [SETUP.md#procedure](SETUP.md#procedure).\\n## Gates\\n\\nA gate is a named check used to determine whether an action meets its required conditions. It contains one or more predicates. A predicate is one exact condition, such as \\u201cthe work order is approved\\u201d or \\u201call declared changed paths are within the permitted scope.\\u201d\\n\\n`harnessctl` evaluates the applicable predicates when a checkpoint is requested, a transition is previewed or applied, or a preparation command runs its required checks. \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-lifecycle-native26-20261010\\\\codex-211\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\reference\\\\server\\\\contracts\\\\lifecycle-v2.md\", \"sha256\": \"4e1707f6664157a9ab47e8b38301090551b35153b91bd10315a41ee39aae2984\", \"bytes\": 5575, \"text\": \"# Private lifecycle rehearsal wire contract\\n\\nThe v2 endpoint accepts only `lifecycle-v2.json`. Every request and result selects\\ntest data. Git remains authoritative for real work. Existing v1 routes and the\\nseven read-only MCP tools keep their contract; they cannot dispatch v2 actions.\\nIn an explicitly configured test project their results use\\n`se-harness-graph-read/v2`, with a required test-copy label. Ordinary Phase 2\\nprojects retain their v1 read result shapes. Revision byte hashing is unchanged;\\ntest revisions add explicit test-copy provenance, without rewriting v1 fixtures.\\n\\n`inspect` accepts check, preflight and validate. `preview` runs a mutation in a\\ndiscarded projection and returns its input digest and complete proposed file\\neffects. `apply` requires that digest, reruns the released checks, and commits\\nthe complete result once. A preview never changes graph state. Actor strings\\nare synthetic test inputs, not authenticated human consent.\\n\\nThe digest binds project/context versions, all selected revision IDs, retained\\nsnapshot, exact command/file inputs, principal and released evaluator identity.\\nMode and operation key are excluded from the preview binding, but included in\\nthe accepted request digest used for principal-scoped retry lookup.\\n\\n## Permitted file effects\\n\\n| Action | Permitted effects in the disposable projection |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| check / preflight / validate | No file writes |\\n| transition | Only selected newly authored artifacts and evaluator sidecars declared by their records |\\n| decide | Selected new decision and its explicitly linked rehearsal risk |\\n| raise-risk | New risk and optional paired decision at released domain paths |\\n| handoff | Declared bounded file inputs within the selected work order's scope; released handoff packet and evaluator evidence |\\n| capture-verification | New VREC and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n| prepare-release | New RLS and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n\\nHandoff first uses the released procedure's fixed `evidence` preparation command,\\nthen `check --checkpoint handoff --from-git`. It exposes no arbitrary evidence\\ncommand. File inputs cannot alter formal records, harness selection/instructions,\\nGit configuration, hooks, or executables used by the service. The service never\\nruns source tests. The local qualification runner supplies observed test evidence.\\n\\nThe adapter enumerates every regular file before and after the operation. It\\nrejects deletions, links, unexpected paths, missing sidecars, imported-record\\nchanges and evaluator failure before opening an acceptance transaction.\\n\\n## Snapshots and Git\\n\\nEach accepted operation retains an immutable complete snapshot: exact file bytes,\\nself-contained Git history and its source/test-candidate identities. Content\\ndigests bind the snapshot to the resulting baseline. Context heads, artifact\\nrevisions, snapshot and receipt share one database transaction. Temporary Git\\nrepositories are discarded after the result is accepted or refused.\\n\\nCapture first commits the exact input projection as test candidate P. P excludes\\nthe new VREC. The output retains the input hosted baseline B, source fixture S,\\nP and evaluator identity. Actual implementation candidate C is recorded separately\\nby qualification. Subsequent commits never alter the candidate stored in a VREC.\\n\\nExport selects an immutable baseline, checks its complete snapshot and Git bundle,\\nand returns exact bounded bytes. The installed client writes only to a new explicit\\ndestination and leaves an incomplete marker until every file hash is checked.\\nNo export writes to or synchronizes an authoritative repository.\\n\\n## Bounds and failure categories\\n\\nKeep 4 MiB requests, 2 MiB responses, 1 MiB individual file inputs, two concurrent\\nprojections, 120-second evaluator calls and 10,000 retained artifact revisions.\\nA pilot snapshot/export that exceeds the response bound is refused atomically.\\nRetained complete snapshots have a separate explicit project count bound of 128.\\nThis is a small private pilot, not an unbounded document store.\\n\\nBoundary/malformed requests, stale inputs, evaluator refusals, invalid output and\\nunknown transport outcomes remain distinct. Read the operation receipt after a\\nlost reply. A changed request under the same accepted key is a conflict. The\\nservice does not automatically rerun a mutation at a newer version.\\n\\n## Bounded Cypher reads\\n\\nThe existing `cypher` MCP/HTTP read selects one exact view. Its request uses the\\nread schema, not the lifecycle command schema. Read the public labels and\\nproperties in [the physical representation](../../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md#physical-representation)\\nbefore selecting a query. `Artifact` and `Revision` are distinct public labels.\\n\\nThe admitted form has one `MATCH` or `OPTIONAL MATCH` path, labelled nodes,\\noptional parameterized property comparisons, `RETURN`, and a numeric `LIMIT`.\\nFor example, with `parameters` containing a selected artifact ID under `artifact`:\\n\\n```cypher\\nMATCH (r:Revision) WHERE r.artifact_id = $artifact RETURN r.artifact_id AS id, r.status AS status LIMIT 10\\n```\\n\\nUse the response's completeness fields with the requested row/byte/depth budget.\\nThis example supplies no project filter: the service binds the selected project\\nand view. Unlabelled nodes, `WITH`, aggregation and arbitrary database syntax are\\nnot part of this small public read form. A rejected query has not completed a read.\\nKeep the exact refusal; consult the documented form before constructing another\\nrequest. Do not weaken query admission or bypass it through a direct database call.\\n\"}]}\r\n",

The delegation MUST name the right, its scope, the granting human,\\nand the receiving human. It MUST be recorded before the delegated decision.\\nThe receiving human MUST decide under their own identity.\\n\\nAn instruction for an agent to apply a recorded human decision delegates the\\nexecution of that command. It does not delegate the decision itself. The\\nagent MUST NOT supply a new answer, broaden the targets, or claim the human\\nmade a decision that was not given.\\n\\nRepository policy MAY require different people for conflicting decisions on\\nthe same candidate. When it does, the same human MUST NOT hold both decisions\\nfor that candidate. A human MUST NOT approve their own architecture decision\\nassessment unless they explicitly hold approval authority for that artifact\\nand the separation rules permit it. Drafting an assessment grants no such\\nright.\\n\\nWhen the accountable human or required authority is absent or ambiguous, stop\\nthe affected decision. State the exact right and artifact needing an owner.\\nDo not substitute an available human or agent merely to fill the field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"f07389fbbe529ad544d8b7d7f18894bfa45f0ec69996c93ed8372416b55ddf91\"}]}]}\r\n",

Read the selected definition and its current state.\\n2. Confirm that its content and evidence match the human's completion decision.\\n3. If completion is already recorded, report that state; do not replay it.\\n4. Preview the exact transition below.\\n5. Inspect every target, actor, gate result, and reported effect.\\n6. Apply the same transition only when it matches the decision and passes.\\n7. Read the artifact and new history entry. Preserve any refusal.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set DEFINITION-ID=implemented --decision DEFINITION-ID=HUMAN --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set DEFINITION-ID=implemented --decision DEFINITION-ID=HUMAN --apply --json\\n```\\n\\nThe selected release does not accept definition IDs in `check`. The transition\\npreview supplies the legality and gate result. Do not change a definition's\\nstate by hand to make it selectable.\\n\\n**Completion:** Completion is recorded on that definition, or the exact\\nrefusal is known. Linked work orders keep their states.\\n\\n**Later use:** Select a related work order by its actual ID and use its current\\n`check` result. A completed definition does not select or start all linked work.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"376e69a74eb756254c8e9cd9feba1818526fb640934cc16cc8ed7e5eda7bb426\"}]}]}\r\n",
